clue.text: What is true about English I love, America being flippant?

indicators.note: the word for what is true goes round the English abbreviation, as if wrapped about it

parts.note: a fact is what is true
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O
US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: Someone asks what holds about English, the self and love when America is being flip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the fact round E; 'love' is the tennis zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A facetious remark is jokey and unserious, just as a flippant one treats something lightly.

clue.text: Wet rubbish? Female in the morning collects a great deal

indicators.note: the outer letters gather up the inner word, holding it between them

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
lots means a great deal

explanation.surface: A woman spends her morning gathering up piles of soggy junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'collects' comes after the two outer pieces, which sit side by side. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage and debris found at sea, so it is rubbish that is wet.

clue.text: Nursery item's function

definitions.meaning: a baby's bed found in a nursery
short for cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: What a piece of nursery furniture is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A cot is a baby's bed, and cot abbreviates cotangent, a trigonometric function in mathematics.

clue.text: Competitor making mistake, not quite among the top people

indicators.note: the word for a mistake stops just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a slip or mistake
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: A contestant blunders while mingling with the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of the mistake; the A-list is the roster of most sought-after celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A trialist is someone taking part in a sporting trial, a competitor for selection.

clue.text: Honour a husband, showing a sort of charm

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A decorated husband displays a certain charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British state honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of Caribbean folk magic, practised with spells and charms.

clue.text: Most hare-brained guy meeting restrictions on entering street

indicators.note: the guy and his restrictions go into the street abbreviation

parts.note: cat is slang for a guy or bloke
ties are restrictions or constraints

explanation.surface: A daft man meets curbs as he walks into the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts both pieces together inside the street abbreviation; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty means scatterbrained or flighty, so the superlative is the most scatterbrained.

clue.text: Place for Jacob's ladder, not hotel plant

indicators.note: the hotel letter is denied, taken out of the place name

parts.note: in Genesis Jacob dreamt of the ladder at Bethel
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The site of a biblical ladder, minus the hotel, is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is the climbing pepper plant whose leaves are chewed with areca nut.

clue.text: Bishop getting uncomfortable becomes spiteful

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
itchy means uncomfortable, irritated

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a prickly discomfort turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitchy is informal for malicious and catty, which is what spiteful means.

clue.text: Agency worker taking time signified outspoken attitude

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker from an agency
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: the word for signified is spoken out loud, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: meant means signified

explanation.surface: A temp who took time off revealed a blunt attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' signals that MEANT, said aloud, is spelt MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperament is a person's disposition or character, their habitual attitude.

clue.text: The foreign boozer, little house in the country

parts.note: le is French for the
a sot is a drunkard
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A French pub and a cottage somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' looks like a British pub but is the drinker, SOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Survive in the open before bad turns

parts.note: out means in the open, exposed

indicators.note: the word for bad turns round, read backwards

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: Getting by outdoors before things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlive someone is to survive them, living longer than they do.

clue.text: A broadcaster in Ireland, female, almost a goddess

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

indicators.note: the word for a female loses its final letter, so it is almost complete

parts.note: miss is a young female

explanation.surface: A female Irish broadcaster is very nearly divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek deity of hunting and the moon.

clue.text: Set against warrant officer, everyone appears insignificant?

indicators.note: everyone is placed next to the officer, set against him

parts.note: SM is a sergeant major, a warrant officer rank
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone opposed to the sergeant major looks unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something small is minor, of little importance.

clue.text: Recognise legend, wacko in peculiar guise

indicators.note: the two words appear disguised, their letters in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Spotting a famous eccentric who has dressed up strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge is to recognise, accepting or admitting the existence of something.

clue.text: Covering church fellows provided with time for memorial slab

parts.note: a hat is a head covering
men means fellows

explanation.surface: Churchmen given time to put a covering over a memorial stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchment is a tablet bearing a deceased person's coat of arms, displayed as a memorial.

clue.text: Seek changes in accommodation for minister and be reasonable

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the minister's house

parts.note: a manse is a minister's house

indicators.note: the letters of seek change their order

explanation.surface: Looking for alterations to the vicarage and being sensible about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the first word to KESE, and 'in' sets that inside the minister's house.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sense is to be logical or reasonable, intelligible.

clue.text: Feeble or calm and collected?

definitions.meaning: ... can also mean without nerves, cool and unflustered

explanation.surface: Is someone weak or simply cool-headed?
explanation.definitionFit: Nerveless has two opposite senses: lacking vigour, or showing no anxiety at all.

clue.text: Holy circle in church a lot

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Holy rings appear a great deal in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is the ring of light painted around a saint's head.

clue.text: Hell, with a group of religious folk creating chaos

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
an order is a religious community such as monks or nuns

explanation.surface: Hell and monks combine to cause mayhem.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is a state of confusion and lack of order, the same as chaos.

clue.text: Continue to be someone foolish

explanation.surface: Carry on being an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Go on means proceed or carry on, and a goon is slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Gulped, giving brief account of what happened when tooth came out?

definitions.text: brief account of what happened when tooth came out?
definitions.meaning: gob is slang for mouth, and the mouth bled when a tooth was pulled

explanation.surface: Someone swallowed hard while telling the story of a tooth extraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Gob is British slang for mouth, so 'gob bled' is a two-word report of the extraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbled means swallowed hastily, a synonym of gulped.

clue.text: Lousy rent — raise various amounts paid in advance

indicators.note: a lousy job is a bad one, so these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A tenant grumbles about a terrible rent increase and advance payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Retainers are fees paid in advance to secure someone's services.

clue.text: Fixed a strip of wood or metal around front of window

indicators.note: the strip goes around the window letter, enclosing it

parts.words: a strip of wood or metal
parts.note: a screed is a strip used as a guide for levelling plaster or concrete

indicators.note: only the first letter of window is used

explanation.surface: A builder fixed a strip of timber round a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives W, and 'around' puts SCREED round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwed means fastened with screws, so attached securely in place.

clue.text: Boy in love is in clover

parts.note: a lad is a boy
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A boy in love is living in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in clover' sounds like the idiom for living well, but clover is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladino is a large-leaved variety of white clover grown for fodder.

clue.text: One making a song and dance, these days, always going on

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
AD, anno domini, marks the present era
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A performer making a fuss that goes on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a song and dance' reads as one idiom for fussing, but splits into the definition and BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a singer of ballads, so someone who makes songs.

clue.text: Regret when school subject is squeezed — money found

indicators.note: the school subject is squeezed into the word for regret

parts.note: rue means regret
PE, physical education, is a school subject

explanation.surface: Sorry that a lesson is cut short, but cash turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and other countries.

clue.text: Swimmer finished poetically, clinching races

indicators.note: the poetic word holds the races tightly in its grip

parts.note: o'er is the poetic form of over, finished
the TT, Tourist Trophy, races are held on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A swimmer finishes, in verse, by winning the races.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is an aquatic mammal that is a strong swimmer.

clue.text: Protester did wrong breaking into vehicle behind back of school

indicators.note: the vehicle comes behind, after, the school letter
the last letter of school is taken
the scrambled letters break into the vehicle word

parts.note: ute is short for utility vehicle, a pickup

indicators.note: the letters of did are put wrong, scrambled

explanation.surface: A demonstrator misbehaved, forcing their way into a car behind a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles the word did to DDI, which goes into the pickup; 'behind' puts that after L. A ute is Australian for a pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were 19th-century workers who protested against machinery; now anyone opposed to new technology.

clue.text: Flats maybe by trail in Cornish town

parts.note: pads are flats, homes, as in a bachelor pad
to tow is to trail behind

explanation.surface: Apartments beside a footpath in a Cornish resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Padstow is a fishing port and resort on the north coast of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Padstow is a harbour town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-west tip.

clue.text: Number in company excessively audible

indicators.note: the word for excessively is heard rather than read, so it is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: A businessperson is overly noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'two's company' names the number of people that make good company.

clue.text: Spaniard to make departure twice?

parts.note: to die is to depart this life
the departing is said a second time with another word for it, go

explanation.surface: A Spaniard decides to leave, then leave again.
explanation.walkthrough: Both DIE and GO mean depart; 'twice' asks for two such words.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego is a common Spanish man's name, so it stands for a typical person from Spain.

clue.text: Something edgy about sport bringing bit of bad language

indicators.note: the edged weapon goes about the word for sport, around it

parts.note: a sword has a sharp edge
to sport clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued remark about sport brings out some cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is the verb, as in sporting a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A swearword is a profanity, an obscene or offensive word.
